summary: Ran `ng update @angular/core@9 @angular/cli@9 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp, which bumped the Angular packages to 9.1.13, the CLI toolchain to 9.1.15, TypeScript to 3.8.3, rxjs to 6.6.7, zone.js to 0.10.2, added tslib, and applied Angular's own migrations (tsconfig files/include restructuring for Ivy, SSR renderModule export in main.ts, aot/budgets additions in angular.json). No related third-party packages required a version bump for this hop. Install and build pass; the test command fails the same way it did at baseline (karma's test target points at a nonexistent root-level `styles.css` instead of `src/styles.css`), so no new regression was introduced.
changes: Upgraded @angular/* packages from 8.1.0 to 9.1.13 and @angular/cli / @angular-devkit/build-angular / @angular/compiler-cli / @angular/language-service to 9.1.x
Upgraded typescript from ~3.4.5 to ~3.8.3, rxjs from ^6.4.0 to ^6.6.7, zone.js from ~0.9.1 to ~0.10.2, @types/node from ~11.10.5 to ^12.11.1, codelyzer from ^5.0.1 to ^5.1.2
Added tslib ^1.10.0 as a direct dependency (required peer of Angular 9 packages)

Angular CLI migrations updated angular.json (added aot: true and an anyComponentStyle budget), restructured src/tsconfig.app.json and src/tsconfig.server.json to use files/include instead of exclude for Ivy, and added the SSR renderModule/renderModuleFactory re-export to src/main.ts
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of `ng update`
manual_followups: npm install still prints peer-dependency warnings for @ngrx/* (^8.5.2) and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0, which declare a peer on @angular/core@^8 or ^7; they were left untouched since this hop's automated detection found no required bump and the build/tests are unaffected, but they should be bumped to their Angular-9-compatible majors in a later hop if not already covered by the plan.

The optional node-sass@4.11.0 dependency still fails to build its native binding on this Node 12 environment (missing python2 / no prebuilt binary for this ABI), same as at baseline; it does not fail npm install because it's an optionalDependency.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target references `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present in the baseline angular.json) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing, but it masks the real spec results and is worth a human fix outside this upgrade.
